title: Finchley teacher arrested for missing indecent assault sentencing
text:

 11 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Press Association Sally-Anne Bowen taught at Christ's College in Finchley Police have arrested a teacher convicted of sexually abusing two pupils at an all-boys school in the late 1980s after she failed to turn up for her sentencing hearing.
 Sally-Anne Bowen, who taught chemistry at Christ's College in Finchley, north London, was in her 20s when she had sex with one pupil up to 30 times and kissed a second boy while the pupils were aged about 14 or 15.
 Her trial heard she wore short tight skirts and flirted in class, with one former pupil comparing her behaviour to "a Sabrina Carpenter video".
 After being convicted earlier this year of seven counts of indecent assault, the 65-year-old was granted bail ahead of Friday's scheduled sentencing hearing.
 'Concerns for welfare'
 But Bowen, of Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, did not turn up to Harrow Crown Court, and Judge Karim Ezzat issued an arrest warrant.
 She could not be found at her home by Metropolitan Police officers on Friday morning, the court heard.
 A Met spokesperson said: "On Friday November 20, officers were made aware that a 65-year-old woman had failed to appear at Harrow Crown Court for sentencing.
 "A warrant was issued for her arrest and officers promptly launched inquiries to locate her.
 "At around 3pm, officers from a neighbouring force found the woman at a location in Hampshire and arrested her on suspicion of failing to appear at court.
 "She has been taken into police custody. A new sentencing date will be set by the court in due course."
 Earlier, prosecutor Neelam Gomersall had said Bowen's partner of 36 years, Darren Scotchbrook, was at the address when officers turned up, but Bowen was not.
 Gomersall told the court that there was "no evidence" Bowen could not attend the sentencing, and information from her partner was "suggestive of refusal rather than inability" to attend.
 Defence barrister Mark Kimsey said: "Our instructing solicitor has tried to contact her and the phone rings but doesn't answer."
 He said that Bowen was in contact with solicitors on Thursday and had engaged with a pre-sentence report, adding there had been "concerns as to her welfare due to the content of the messages" from her.
